title: infra mail dmarc report calls every present-but-failing DKIM result 'your own mail, failing', though aggregate data cannot tell own mail from a forged or unsigned one, and in Prodinfra's archive all five such records are forged or unsigned
body:
FOUND 2026-09-25 by prodinfra-cc, reading Prodinfra's DMARC archive, and ruled into 0.1.8 by hv.

WHAT HAPPENS. `bin/devbin infra mail dmarc parse dmarc/ | bin/devbin infra mail dmarc report` (Prodinfra, vendored runtime 0.1.7 at 142763d, 135 reports) prints every record whose DKIM signature is present but not passing under the heading "DKIM PRESENT BUT NOT PASSING -- your own mail, failing" (5 records: geodica.com from 198.44.49.217, 35 msgs and 1 msg; ficton.net from 212.146.165.173, 202.164.207.194 and 103.186.57.35, 1 msg each; all dkim=fail spf=softfail).

NONE OF THEM IS THE DOMAIN'S OWN MAIL:
- geodica.com, Google report 7207663151206468299, 14 Sep window: dkim_auth [{domain: geodica.com, selector: dkim, result: fail}], SPF softfail, from 198.44.49.217 (Hostwinds/HostPapa). geodica.com's only DKIM key is at selector `google`; it publishes none at `dkim`. The signature is forged.
- ficton.net, docomo.ne.jp reports 9a5b89d56164c12a3eaa1c48542edace and fa45eb87778bf3efeaf46a0d2816bb60: dkim_auth [{domain: "", selector: "", result: fail}]. With no signing domain, nothing ties these messages to ficton.net's mail.

THE DEFECT. The heading claims an ownership that aggregate data cannot establish. A signature that is present and failing is either the domain's own mail broken in transit or a forged signature, and the report has no profile to tell the two apart. Its own WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE section says as much about passing signatures. The label sent the reader looking for a broken geodica.com sender that does not exist.

WHAT A FIX MUST DO:
- report: the heading names both readings and claims neither, eg "DKIM PRESENT BUT NOT PASSING -- own mail broken in transit, or a forged signature". Each row prints its signing domain and selector, an empty one named as none, so the reader can tell which.
- check, which has the profile: a failing signature whose selector the profile does not declare for that domain (0143's labelled DKIM records), or whose signing domain is empty or not the domain's, is called out as not the domain's declared key. A failing signature on a declared selector stays the own-mail case.
- WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE on the report says the report cannot tell own mail from forged, and names check as the command that can.
- Arms, each red first: the heading over a forged-selector row and an unsigned row, with the domain and selector printed; check's call-out over an undeclared selector and an empty signer, with a control on a declared selector. Mutants for each. The page: infra.md, wherever the report's sections and check's DMARC rows are described.

vc's. It ships in 0.1.8, built on 0143 (the labelled DKIM records) and 0142 (the shared fake).

## Resolution

Fixed at 6e9b1bb, the report fix only, on hv's ruling. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. The heading reads "DKIM PRESENT BUT NOT PASSING -- own mail broken in transit, or a forged signature", claiming neither, since aggregate data cannot say which. Every row with a signature prints each one as `<result> d=<signing domain> s=<selector>`, comma-joined where a record carries several, an empty field as `none` and a selector the report left out as `absent`, so a forged selector and the domain's own key no longer read the same; a record with no signature still reads `dkim=absent`. WHAT THIS CANNOT SEE says the report cannot tell own mail from forged, that the way to tell is to compare the row's d= and s= with the selectors the domain publishes, and that a profile-aware infra mail dmarc check is planned (devbin's ST0006). infra.md says all of it.
- NOT HERE, ON hv's RULING (2026-09-25). The check half of the issue -- a verb reading the rows beside the profile and calling out a failing signature on a key the profile does not declare -- is ST0006 WP-02, and ST0006 waits for hv's word. v1 built it; v2 leaves it, with every refactor only it needed, to that work package, and v1 is kept for it. The 0121 arm still holds that `dmarc check` does not dispatch, and now reads the report's planned line too, so the line cannot outlive the verb's arrival unnoticed.
- REVIEWS. critic-shell reviewed the code and test-checked the arms, with no critical finding; each point taken, and the commit message names them. vc's review: vc, 2026-09-25, approved at v2 on hv's ruling, the patch and the evidence below, including the widened 0121 arm.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Every 0147 arm red at the 0143 base at its own assertion, over rows-signers.jsonl, a new fixture in Prodinfra's shapes on documentation domains; the dkim=absent guard green there by design. 12 mutants, each against its own arm: 12 of 12 killed.
- THE SUITE. All of tests/unit over the nine 0.1.8 changes stacked in landing order on b10dd41 (0139, 0128, 0133, 0130, 0142, 0143, 0144, 0146, 0147), on a clean checkout (head 308cf21), 2026-09-25 11:34:20Z to 12:09:20Z: 1907 of 1907 ok, 0 not ok, no gaps, its 5 skips the suite's declared ones. Main after the landing is byte-identical to that tree outside intent/.
